text: Qing Bao Tian Zun's schemes have now succeeded, and the great Bastion forged by the Dragon Emperor has collapsed. Chaos lurks beyond, the Dragon's children war among themselves within, and rebellions rise throughout the Empire. General Han Peng still holds Po Mei alone, while General Fu must break through the encircling Chaos as swiftly as possible, restore the Great Bastion, sweep away the taint of evil, and return peace to Cathay.

Though the Great Bastion has been reclaimed, its power to ward off evil and impurity has been lost. To bring Cathay back to peace, one must journey to the Chaos Wastes, using the Celestial Tower as a medium to channel the Dragon Emperor's might and restore the Bastion anew.\\nAccording to the calculations of the Celestial Officials, the nodes for building the Celestial Tower lie in the farthest north and farthest south, places where the Winds of Magic rage so fiercely that ordinary men can scarcely survive—yet which are of great benefit to the ritual. Take care, however, for the ancient great enemy Kairos Fateweaver has also learned of this, and will surely do everything in his power to hinder you.

For a long time, the Crow-Folk had secretly sought a Child of Prophecy according to the omens they had divined—one said to be destined to bring utter ruin to Cathay. In the end, their gaze fell upon a general of the Great Bastion: Xin Wu.\\nXin Wu fought bravely, cared for his subordinates, cherished the people of Cathay, and his loyalty was beyond reproach—for these reasons he was deeply beloved, and regarded by all as the natural successor to command the Great Bastion.\\nUntil, during a Chaos incursion, in order to reverse a collapsing battle line, Xin Wu single-handedly charged into the heart of the enemy formation, dueled their chieftain, and perished alongside him. But even as all mourned Xin Wu's death, he miraculously returned to life.\\nHis feats of arms and his miraculous resurrection earned him unmatched devotion within the army—but this only confirmed the Crow-Folk's suspicions. Xin Wu was indeed the one prophesied to bring ruin upon Cathay.\\nSoon, he and his soldiers were surrounded by the Celestial Dragon Guard, led by General Hao Tian, who had rushed to the scene. Facing Xin Wu's furious and uncomprehending gaze, General Hao Tian, with the detached coldness of a god, revealed the contents of the prophecy.\\nHaving learned the truth, Xin Wu chose to cease resistance, offering himself willingly for execution by General Hao Tian, and ordered his soldiers, who sought to defend him, to lay down their arms. But after the execution, General Hao Tian broke his promise to Xin Wu that the others would be spared.\\nIn the name of utterly eradicating Chaos's influence, General Hao Tian gave the order to attack. The soldiers who had laid down their weapons were nothing but lambs before the Celestial Dragon Guard General Hao Tian had brought. This was not war—it was pure slaughter.\\nRegret and unyielding fury swept through the fading consciousness of Xin Wu, who lay dying, powerless to stop it, his mind sinking irreversibly into an eternal, cold, and solitary darkness. It was then that the voices of the Four Powers spoke in his ear. They granted Xin Wu strength, on the condition that once his vengeance was complete, they would claim the use of his body.\\nReborn amid blood and fire, Xin Wu delivered brutal death upon his enemies. Almost none survived that battle. With blood soaking his hands, Xin Wu could no longer call himself a protector.\\nXin Wu, who dared defy the Celestial Court, became a banner for rebellion. The rule of the Dragons was far from perfect—their plans, measured in spans of centuries, had brought endless suffering to the people of the present, the construction of the Grand Canal being but one example.\\nAs Xin Wu won victory after victory, nobles, merchants, soldiers, rebels, and even Dragonkin flocked to his cause, as numerous as the trees of Kun Lan. He now held sway over a third of Cathay—a force even the Dragon's children could not afford to dismiss lightly.\\nIndeed, Miao Ying personally led Cathay's most elite garrison forces southward, while Zhao Ming blocked his path northward. But by then, Xin Wu had come to possess an artifact rivaling even the might of the Dragons—the Defier of Fate, a gift bestowed by the Four Powers, capable of severing the threads of fate and delivering destined death to all things.\\nQing Bao Tian Zun's disciples worked tirelessly to paint for Xin Wu a vision of a future Cathay ruled not by dragons but by mortals themselves, requiring only that he sweep away the Dragon's children who had usurped the throne. Many rallied to this vision, and just as many opposed it—never had Cathay been so divided. And as the storm within Cathay was gradually fanned into shape by the Spirit Raven, the armies of Chaos had already gathered quietly north of the Great Bastion.\\nBut when the Chaos horde broke through Long Men Pass, what awaited them was not the battered remnants of Xin Wu and Miao Ying's clash, but the spears of both armies raised together against them.\\nUnexpectedly, Xin Wu had reached a secret pact with Miao Ying before the battle, agreeing to work together to unravel Chaos's schemes, and taking upon himself the burden of the war of attrition. Though Xin Wu achieved great victories in this battle, the soldiers loyal to him suffered heavy losses. But paying this blood-price to earn Cathay's renewed acceptance was itself part of the pact.\\nAfter the battle, Miao Ying swore in the name of the Hao Tian Dragon Emperor that Cathay would never seek retribution against Xin Wu's followers.\\nXin Wu then took up his divine sword, the Defier of Fate—capable of delivering death to all things—and turned it upon himself, refusing in this manner to pay the price owed to the Four Powers. A group of his most loyal followers likewise took their own lives alongside him.\\nIn the years that followed, this history was twisted into an absurd myth, known truly only to the ancestral sages who guard Xin Wu's body. They understood deeply that the might of the Four Powers was unfathomable, and that this was not the end—that prophecy still clung to Cathay like a maggot buried in bone.\\nAnd now, that same Xin Wu, who once cast a terrible shadow over Cathay, has been resurrected once more through the machinations of Qing Bao Tian Zun, come again to bring ruin upon Cathay.

You fought desperately to hold Xin Wu's attention, buying Qu Miao Ying the chance she needed to unravel the magic controlling him. Just as his blade—vast as one wielded by a giant—was about to fall upon your brow, it stopped short, the wake of its passage forming a storm of its own. Then Xin Wu let out a furious roar, tearing every Chaos soldier present to shreds.\\nWhen it was over, Xin Wu learned from your own words the current state of Cathay. He vowed that, when the moment was right, he would lend you his aid.
